title: Does salt make pasta water boil faster?
hook: Dissolving salt raises water’s boiling point. The size of the effect depends on concentration.
summary: Salt raises the boiling point: 29.2 grams per kilogram of water increase the boiling temperature by about 0.5 °C.
cardText: No. Salt raises the boiling point: 29.2 grams per kilogram of water add about 0.5 °C. Adding flavor to pasta is one reason to use it.

cardBlocks.text: Dissolving salt in water raises its boiling point, an effect called boiling-point elevation. The size of this increase depends on concentration: 29.2 grams of salt in one kilogram of water raise the boiling temperature by about 0.5 °C. With salt present, the water needs a higher temperature to boil.

So why does boiling intensify when salt falls into water that is already boiling? The grains give steam bubbles easy places to form. This burst of bubbles does not mean salt lowered the boiling point. Adding flavor to pasta is one reason to add salt to its water.
With 29.2 grams of salt per kilogram of water, the boiling point rises by about 0.5 °C.

deepDiveBlocks.text: How much salt would it take?

The effect depends on the number of dissolved particles. To raise the boiling point by 1 °C, you would need to dissolve almost 60 grams of salt per liter, far saltier than seawater, which is about 3.5% salt by weight.
Dissolved salt also lowers water’s freezing point, and by more: the 29 grams per kilogram that raise the boiling point by 0.5 °C lower the freezing point by almost 2 °C.
The burst of bubbles when salt is added is called nucleation: solid grains, such as salt or sugar crystals, make it easier for bubbles to form in water that is already boiling.

claims.text: Salt does not make water boil faster: dissolving it slightly raises water’s boiling point.

support.excerpt: In fact, adding salt does the very opposite of making water boil faster. Instead, it makes it take longer for the water to boil!
The salt actually increases the boiling point of the water
Some people believe that the addition of salt increases the boiling point of the water. Technically, they are correct, but the increase is rather small.
